item.title: Desk 01 • Statutory Directive • Supreme Court Restores Customs Appellate Tribunal Ruling: Sets Aside High Court Order and Holds Tribunal Is Final Arbiter of Facts While Valuation Must Strictly Follow Section 25 Sequence
item.description: Landmark judgment authored by Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi and concurred by CJ Yahya Afridi and Justice Irfan Saadat Khan restores judgment authored by Mr Muhammad Iqbal Bhawana, Member Technical; holds High Court reference jurisdiction cannot disturb findings of fact absent proof of perversity, and bars direct resort to Section 25(9) fall-back valuation. In a landmark, path-breaking judgment that decisively redefines customs jurisprudence and curbs administrative overreach across Pakistan, the Supreme Court of Pakistan has set aside a Division Bench order of the Sindh High Court and fully restored the common judgment of the Customs Appellate Tribunal, Karachi Bench, authored by Mr Muhammad Iqbal Bhawana, Member Technical. The judgment was authored by Mr Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi on behalf of a three-member appellate bench that included Chief Justice Yahya Afridi and Mr Justice Irfan Saadat Khan, disposing of 24 consolidated petitions (Civil Petitions Nos. 306-K to 329-K of 2024) filed by commercial importers of tyres and tubes. The apex court held in unambiguous and categorical terms that the Customs Appellate Tribunal is the final fact-finding forum in tax and customs matters under the statutory scheme of the Customs Act, 1969. The Supreme Court declared that the reference jurisdiction of the High Court under Section 196 is strictly limited to answering substantial questions of law, and the High Court possesses no legal authority to go behind, re-examine, or substitute findings of fact recorded by the Tribunal unless a specific question of law is competently framed establishing that the Tribunal's findings are perverse, based on surmises and conjectures, or entirely unsupported by evidence on record. item.title: Desk 02 • Bilateral Capital & Banking • Provincial Revenue Authorities SRB, PRA, KPRA and BRA Harmonize Digital Sales Tax on Services via Single-Portal Tax Return Architecture
item.description: Historic inter-provincial accord establishes unified electronic filing framework, synchronized input tax credit verification, and automated cross-jurisdictional withholding reconciliations across all four federating units. In a transformative milestone for Pakistan's fiscal decentralization and ease of doing business, the four provincial revenue bodies—the Sindh Revenue Board (SRB), the Punjab Revenue Authority (PRA), the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Revenue Authority (KPRA), and the Balochistan Revenue Authority (BRA)—have finalized the operational rollout of a unified single-portal tax return architecture for sales tax on services. Spearheaded under the National Tax Council's coordination framework, the platform resolves decades-old inter-provincial withholding friction, eliminate double taxation, and simplifies statutory compliance for nationwide corporate taxpayers. The harmonized framework establishes standardized taxable service definitions across telecommunications, corporate logistics, software development, insurance, and construction. Under the new digital workflow, corporate entities operating nationwide can file a consolidated monthly electronic return through a single window, with automated software splitting and transmitting tax shares directly to the respective provincial exchequers according to origin-and-destination principles agreed upon by provincial finance ministries.

item.description: Frontier research lab rolls out next-generation 5.5 architecture featuring native sub-second multi-turn reasoning, multi-file agentic code synthesis, and enterprise-grade sandboxed runtime verification. item.title: Desk 05 • Aviation & Multilateral Diplomacy • Neelum Valley Sharda Peeth Cultural Corridor Radiates Autumn Splendour as Eco-Tourism and Heritage Restoration Preserve Ancient Seat of Learning
item.description: Azad Kashmir’s historic Sharda temple and university ruins draw cultural historians and alpine trekkers; sustainable eco-lodges in Arang Kel and Keran ensure ecological preservation across pristine Himalayan border valleys. item.title: Desk 06 • Monday Night Football & Astrophysics • Manchester City Suffer Shock 1-2 Defeat Against Aston Villa as Resilient Fulham Edge Coventry City 2-1 in Saturday Action
item.description: Defending champions stunned after second-half defensive lapse against Unai Emery's side; Fulham secure vital three points over spirited Coventry City; Premier League title race blown wide open. In a stunning turn of events that sent shockwaves through the English Premier League, defending champions Manchester City suffered a shock 1-2 defeat against Unai Emery's high-flying Aston Villa on Saturday afternoon. Despite controlling territorial possession with 74 percent of the ball, Pep Guardiola's side appeared uncharacteristically sluggish in transition and were repeatedly unpicked by incisive, high-tempo counter-attacks. City had initially pressed forward in numbers during the opening quarter, but failed to capitalize on early set-piece opportunities, leaving vulnerable space behind their advanced wing-backs. Aston Villa broke the deadlock midway through the first half with a clinical breakaway finish into the bottom corner, exposing a fractured City backline. Although Manchester City responded with furious waves of pressure and pulled level early in the second half when a driven low cross was turned into the net from close range, defensive fragility returned to haunt the champions. In the 78th minute, a swift turnover in midfield allowed Villa's forward line to carve open the penalty area, clinically slotting home the 2-1 winner off the inside of the far upright past an outstretched Ederson.

item.title: Desk 01 • Statutory Directive • FBR Issues Customs General Order No. 06 of 2026 Operationalizing Monthly Installment Facility for Sales Tax on Imported Mobile Phones via DIRBS Framework
item.description: Revenue Division amends Ninth Schedule of Sales Tax Act 1990; tax liabilities partitioned into equal monthly installments through June 30 fiscal deadline; automated DIRBS blocking enforced upon non-payment. The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) in coordination with the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has formally operationalized Customs General Order (CGO) No. 06 of 2026, establishing a standardized procedure that permits individual consumers to pay sales tax liabilities on imported cellular devices in monthly installments through the Device Identification, Registration and Blocking System (DIRBS). Promulgated pursuant to statutory amendments to the Ninth Schedule of the Sales Tax Act, 1990, the framework dismantles upfront capital friction on high-duty mobile devices while institutionalizing verifiable digital revenue tracking across the national telecom sector. Under the notified regulatory architecture, an applicant’s aggregate sales tax assessment is divided into equal monthly installments corresponding to the number of months remaining in the active financial year, terminating strictly on June 30. Consumers register the international mobile equipment identity (IMEI) on the DIRBS portal and discharge the initial installment via an automatically generated Payment Slip ID (PSID), which grants immediate temporary cellular network activation. Subsequent installments fall due on the corresponding date of each succeeding month, supported by automated digital payment notifications integrated with 1Link interbank banking switches.

item.title: Desk 05 • Aviation & Multilateral Diplomacy • Autumn Foliage Transforms Pakistan's Northern Valleys as Neelum and Hunza Experience Surge in Cultural and Archaeological Tourism
item.description: Poplar canopies turn brilliant amber across Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir; Sharda Peeth conservation initiative in Neelum Valley complements crisp alpine hiking trails in Swat and Kaghan. item.description: Second-highest successful run chase in ODI history unfolds at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium as Pavan Rathnayake's 130 and Janith Liyanage's unbeaten 61* seal sensational two-wicket triumph with one ball to spare. item.title: Desk 01 • Statutory Directive • FBR Fast-Tracks National Faceless Centre Deployment as IMF Urges Multi-Year Policy Predictability Over Ad-Hoc Surcharges
item.description: National Faceless Centre in Islamabad deploys algorithmic third-party data matching across hundreds of thousands of non-filers; IMF-Finance Ministry workshop calls for structural base-broadening and investment certainty. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) Chairman Rashid Mehmood Langrial directed the immediate operational acceleration of the newly established National Faceless Centre (NFC) in Islamabad on Tuesday, 20 October 2026. Designed as the technological spearhead of Pakistan's direct-tax overhaul, the NFC has initiated pilot automated audits by running third-party financial data—drawn from real estate transfers, motor vehicle purchases, international travel ledgers, and commercial electricity consumption—against national tax declaration rolls. By decoupling assessment powers from geographical jurisdictions and field officer discretion, the faceless model aims to eliminate arbitrary physical interfaces and institutionalize objective algorithmic audit scrutiny across high-net-worth non-filers. The administrative push coincides with a high-level two-day joint workshop convened in Islamabad on 20–21 October 2026 by the Ministry of Finance and the International Monetary Fund (IMF), bringing together senior multilateral tax economists, provincial finance secretaries, and international revenue specialists. Opening the plenary sessions, IMF mission representatives urged Pakistani fiscal authorities to decisively move beyond short-term revenue surcharges and advance-tax withholding levies, calling instead for a transparent, multi-year statutory tax architecture that broadens the base while offering long-term policy certainty to domestic and foreign industrial investors.

Future Tech Markets reports that at CoreWeave's Fully Connected enterprise event in San Francisco, specialized cloud provider CoreWeave announced the commercial availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale systems powered by Spectrum-X 102.4T Ethernet networking. Cognition, the AI laboratory behind the autonomous software engineering agent Devin, has become the first commercial customer running live production workloads on Vera Rubin hardware. CoreWeave also launched NVIDIA Vera, introduced as the industry's first dedicated central processor engineered specifically for autonomous AI agents, alongside CoreWeave Forge—a unified platform for training, evaluating, and fine-tuning agentic models. item.title: Desk 04 • Studio Regulation & Music Charts • Jessica Chastain Horror 'Other Mommy' Tops Thursday Previews with $3.6M, Projecting $28M Opening Weekend to Dethrone 'Verity'
item.description: Universal and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster title opens across 2,850 screens as Colleen Hoover adaptation 'Verity' holds second place with $13.3M frame; Aaron Sorkin's 'The Social Reckoning' stumbles. Variety and Media Digest report that Universal Pictures and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster's psychological horror thriller 'Other Mommy', starring Oscar winner Jessica Chastain, captured $3.6 million in domestic Thursday preview screenings across 2,850 theaters. Industry tracking projects the horror feature to generate between $22 million and $28 million over its three-day opening weekend, with bullish estimates reaching $35 million as word-of-mouth spreads across genre audiences. The strong opening is expected to dislodge last weekend's box office leader, the Amazon MGM Colleen Hoover adaptation 'Verity', which is projected to hold the second position with approximately $13.3 million. Early distributor estimates from Media Digest place 'Other Mommy' at $27.5 million from 3,365 weekend locations, establishing strong commercial momentum for horror cinema heading into mid-October.

item.title: Desk 05 • Aviation & Multilateral Diplomacy • Third Chitral Expo 2026 Opens at Pamir Riverside Inn as TDAP and Chitral Chamber Showcase Gemstones, Dry Fruits and Mountain Tourism
item.description: Two-day regional trade showcase features Chitrali handicrafts, honey, minerals, and B2B investor summits; Gilgit-Baltistan allocates Rs7 billion to Youth Development Programme for tourism scholarships. Dawn and The Nation report that the 3rd Chitral Expo 2026 officially commenced today at the Pamir Riverside Inn in Chitral. Organized by the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan (TDAP) Peshawar in collaboration with the Chitral Chamber of Commerce & Industry, the two-day event showcases northern Pakistan's finest indigenous products—including handcrafted Chitrali Patti, organic dry fruits, natural honey, cut gemstones, and rare minerals. The expo features high-level B2B networking sessions bringing together international buyers, export houses, and hospitality entrepreneurs to stimulate private capital investment in the Hindu Kush region. In addition to commodity exhibits, the summit spotlights Chitral's immense eco-tourism and agro-processing potential, with the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa scheduled to preside as chief guest at the concluding ceremony on October 11.

item.title: Desk 06 • Monday Night Football & Astrophysics • Farhan's 89 and Sadaqat's 50 Chase Down 183 as Pakistan Beat Sri Lanka by Four Wickets in First T20I at Rawalpindi
item.description: Captain Sahibzada Farhan strikes 10 fours and 4 sixes in match-winning 92-run partnership; Hubert Hurkacz stuns Novak Djokovic 6-4 6-3 in Shanghai while Elise Mertens upsets Iga Swiatek in Beijing. Dawn and ESPNcricinfo report that Pakistan secured a thrilling four-wicket victory over Sri Lanka with seven balls to spare in the opening T20 International at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, chasing down a challenging target of 183 to reach 187-6 in 18.5 overs. Leading the national side in his first match as full-time T20I captain, Sahibzada Farhan played a magnificent captain's knock of 89 off just 53 balls, hammering 10 boundaries and 4 towering sixes. Farhan was ably supported by Maaz Sadaqat, who blasted a rapid half-century (50 off 29 balls) during a match-defining 92-run second-wicket partnership. Earlier, Sri Lanka posted 182-8 in their allotted 20 overs on the back of Lahiru Udara's resilient 91 off 55 balls. For Pakistan, pace spearhead Naseem Shah returned figures of 3-36, while debutant Mohammad Imran impressed with 2-21 as Pakistan took a 1-0 lead in the three-match series ahead of the second T20I on October 11.

item.title: Desk 01 • Statutory Directive • Lahore High Court Summons FBR Chairman and Customs Leadership on Smart Wearable Tech Imports as Return Filings Cross 5.82 Million Under Extended 15 October Window
item.description: Chief Justice orders top tax, customs, and commerce officials to submit statutory policy on camera-equipped wearables by 15 October; revenue authorities accelerate EFS livestock track and IRIS electronic processing as IMF unlocks $1.2B tranche. Business Recorder reports that the Lahore High Court (LHC) has directed federal regulatory leadership—including the Chairman of the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), the Member of Customs, the Interior Secretary, and the Commerce Secretary—to appear in person on 15 October 2026 in a constitutional petition examining the commercial import, tariff classification, and privacy framework for camera-equipped smart glasses and wearable computing devices. Presided over by Chief Justice Aaliya Neelum, the bench expressed concern over the delayed submission of coordinated policy guidelines between Pakistan Customs, the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), and the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA). The judicial directives require the statutory bodies to clarify whether imported smart wearables equipped with integrated optical sensors and artificial intelligence processors should be classified under standard consumer eyewear tariffs or subjected to specialized telecommunication security clearances under the Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-organization) Act, 1996, and Section 25A of the Customs Act, 1969. The court emphasized that without unified classification and import standards, commercial consignments risk arbitrary detention at port terminals while fundamental citizen privacy rights remain vulnerable to unregulated recording hardware.

item.title: Desk 05 • Aviation & Multilateral Diplomacy • Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Earns Record Rs335.7 Million from Markhor Trophy Auction as FWO Completes 115-KM All-Weather Skardu-Astor Highway
item.description: Chitral's Toshi-II markhor permit fetches historic $335,600 with 80% proceeds channeled to local village conservation committees while autumn foliage peaks across Gilgit-Baltistan and Neelum Valley. The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Wildlife Department recorded a historic milestone on Thursday, generating an unprecedented Rs335.69 million ($1.21 million) from the auction of four community-based markhor trophy hunting permits for the 2026-27 season. Conducted transparently in Peshawar, the auction saw the coveted Toshi-II permit in Chitral fetch an all-time record bid of $335,600, while the Toshi-I permit sold for $301,000, Gehret Chitral for $291,000, and Kaigah Kohistan for $284,000. Under established community conservation rules, 80 percent of auction proceeds are disbursed directly to local village conservation committees to fund mountain schools, solar microgrids, and watershed protection. Simultaneously, the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) announced the formal completion and commissioning of a vital new 115-kilometer all-weather strategic highway linking Skardu and Astor through difficult glacial terrain. The newly paved highway slashes transit times from seven hours to less than three hours, creating a resilient economic corridor for agricultural freight and tourism between Baltistan and the Karakoram Highway.

item.title: Desk 01 • Statutory Directive • FBR Drafts Export Facilitation Scheme Track for Imported Livestock and Meat Under SRO 1752(I)/2026
item.description: Board opens duty-free import of live animals for domestic fattening and value-added meat re-export, establishing quarantine tracking and electronic audit trails under amended Customs Rules 2001. The Federal Board of Revenue has proposed bringing meat and imported live animals under the Export Facilitation Scheme (EFS), allowing livestock operators and commercial slaughterhouses to import cattle, sheep and goats free of customs duty, additional customs duty and regulatory duty for fattening and re-export. The breakthrough proposal, notified through draft SRO 1752(I)/2026 amending the Customs Rules, 2001, opens two distinct operational tracks designed to position Pakistan as a leading meat processing hub for GCC and Middle Eastern halal markets. Under the draft framework, Track A governs the import of live animals strictly for domestic fattening at certified animal holding facilities prior to slaughter and export as chilled or frozen meat. Track B permits licensed abattoirs and meat processors to import animals for immediate slaughter and cold-chain value addition. Both pathways require mandatory integration with the Pakistan Single Window (PSW) and the Board's electronic WeBOC platform, establishing end-to-end cargo traceability from the port of discharge to the registered export consignment.

item.title: Desk 03 • Frontier Architectures • OpenAI Releases 722 Formal Mathematical Manuscripts Generated by Internal Frontier Model via Lean 4 Verification
item.description: Research repository openai/math catalogs solutions to open conjectures, averaging three hours of ChatGPT Pro compute per proof and igniting global debate on machine discovery. item.description: Crime-thriller sequel achieves Rs222 crore domestic net and reaches Rs341 crore worldwide; Sacnilk reports highest first-Monday retention in modern Bollywood history. Abhishek Pathak's suspense thriller 'Drishyam 3: The Conclusion', starring Ajay Devgn, Tabu, and Jaideep Ahlawat, has delivered a seismic theatrical performance across domestic and overseas territories, grossing over Rs222 crore net in India across its first five days of release and pushing its cumulative worldwide gross past Rs341 crore. item.title: Desk 05 • Aviation & Multilateral Diplomacy • US Diplomatic Mission Visits Skardu and Satpara Dam as Gilgit-Baltistan Activates Glacier Protection Framework
item.description: Chargé d'Affaires Natalie Baker inspects clean hydel infrastructure; Chief Minister Amjad Hussain coordinates international partnerships for high-altitude climate resilience. United States Chargé d'Affaires Natalie A. Baker concluded a landmark official working visit to Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan on Wednesday, holding comprehensive discussions with Governor Syed Mehdi Shah and regional development authorities on clean energy, sustainable alpine tourism, water security, and climate adaptation across the northern frontier. During the high-level engagement, discussions focused on scaling bilateral cooperation to protect fragile glaciated valleys while expanding regional economic opportunities for local communities. A central component of the diplomatic itinerary included an extensive technical inspection of the Satpara Dam project, located four kilometers south of Skardu town. Authorities briefed the delegation on the multi-purpose dam's operational capacity, which impounds 93,000 acre-feet of glacial meltwater from the Satpara Stream, generating 17.3 megawatts of clean hydroelectricity while supplying over 3 million gallons of potable water daily to municipal reservoirs and irrigating 15,000 acres of fertile agricultural land in the Skardu valley.

item.title: Desk 06 • Monday Night Football & Astrophysics • Iga Swiatek Dismantles Iva Jovic 6-1, 6-3 to Reach China Open Quarter-Finals as Elise Mertens Topples Coco Gauff
item.description: World No. 2 breaks four times in clinical 95-minute masterclass; Belgium's Mertens ends five-match losing streak against Gauff to set up blockbuster Beijing clash. World No. 2 Iga Swiatek produced an emphatic display of baseline precision to dismantle 18-year-old American qualifier Iva Jovic 6-1, 6-3 on Wednesday, securing her place in the quarter-finals of the China Open (WTA 1000) at the National Tennis Center in Beijing. The 2023 champion required just 1 hour and 35 minutes to assert complete authority on Diamond Court, firing 24 baseline winners, winning 76% of her first-service points, and converting four of seven break points in a flawless performance. Swiatek's clinical victory sets up a high-profile quarter-final showdown against Belgium's No. 13 seed Elise Mertens, who produced the upset of the tournament by eliminating defending champion and world No. 4 Coco Gauff in straight sets, 6-3, 6-3. Mertens, who had lost all five of her previous meetings against the American, capitalized ruthlessly on Gauff's unforced errors—including eight double faults—winning 10 of the final 11 points to reach her maiden Beijing quarter-final in seven tournament appearances.

item.title: Desk 01 • Statutory Directive • Federal Board of Revenue Outperforms Q1 Benchmark Surpassing Rs3,083 Billion as IMF Review Finalizes $1.2 Billion Tranche
item.description: Inland revenue collections exceed statutory target by Rs30 billion while electronic returns on IRIS 3.0 surpass 5.8 million declarations; technical deliberations validate fiscal trajectory ahead of 15 October filing cloture. item.description: SRB, PRA, KPRA, and BRA establish unified electronic withholding schedules while SECP unveils accreditation standards for corporate liquidators; PSX KSE-100 consolidates at 165,867 points amid heavy blue-chip volumes. Under the newly prescribed statutory mechanism, taxable income is determined by deducting allowable operational expenses from total gross remuneration, with expenses strictly capped at a statutory ceiling of 30% of total revenue. Total remuneration is legally defined as the higher of actual remuneration received (whether in cash or in kind) or the figure computed under a prescribed Revenue-Per-Mille (RPM) formula. The revenue authority established an initial benchmark RPM of Rs195 per 1,000 YouTube video views, requiring taxpayers who claim lower actual earnings to submit auditable electronic platform statements to the satisfaction of the Commissioner Inland Revenue.

item.description: Asian Development Bank projects 8.3% inflation and economic acceleration supported by manufacturing recovery; federal authorities reduce petrol and diesel prices by up to Rs3.12/litre while directing field commissioners to expand retail tax documentation. item.title: Desk 01 • Statutory Directive • FBR Enforces Parametric Computerized Audit Selection Policy for Tax Year 2026 Under Section 214C and Mandates Automated IRIS Compliance Questionnaires

item.title: Desk 01 • Statutory Directive • State Bank Liquid Reserves Touch $21.39 Billion on $3.06 Billion Eurobond Inflow as National Foreign Exchange Buffer Hits $26.79 Billion
item.description: Central bank import cover surpasses three months for first time since 2020; SRO 1495(I)/2026 amends Second Schedule rules ahead of statutory September 30 return deadline. Total liquid foreign exchange reserves held by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) have expanded sharply to $21.389 billion, propelling the country's aggregate national foreign currency buffer—including commercial bank deposits—to an unprecedented $26.791 billion. The central bank confirmed an extraordinary single-week jump of $3.061 billion, primarily driven by the successful financial settlement and proceeds receipt from Pakistan's newly placed sovereign Eurobond issuance alongside sustained expatriate remittance flows. This substantial accumulation of foreign exchange has pushed sovereign import cover comfortably above three full months, establishing a durable structural safety buffer that Pakistan has not consistently maintained since early 2020. The milestone completely dispels sovereign balance-of-payments anxieties, lowers debt refinancing premiums in international secondary capital markets, and provides the Monetary Policy Committee with expanded monetary stability to support industrial investment across the country.

item.title: Desk 02 • Harmonized Compliance • Provincial Revenue Authorities Mobilize Record Rs768 Billion in First-Quarter Receipts Through Digital STS Harmonization
item.description: Sindh Revenue Board, Punjab Revenue Authority, KPRA, and BRA deploy real-time point-of-sale telemetry across 45 commercial districts, establishing unified digital audit trails for services taxation. item.description: Crisp mountain weather welcomes international cultural expeditions across Karakoram valleys; Lowari route to Chitral and Kalash valleys upgraded with eco-tourism infrastructure. item.title: Desk 01 • Statutory Directive • Pakistan Sovereign Foreign Exchange Reserves Surge to Four-Year Record of $21.4 Billion as SBP and Interbank Inflows Bolster Import Cover
item.description: Central bank and commercial banking liquid reserves touch landmark high on $3B monthly remittances and RDA surge; Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and SBP bulletin confirm balance-of-payments stabilization. item.description: "Father Time always wins": The 96-year-old legendary investor formally relinquishes executive stewardship of the $1 trillion conglomerate; Wall Street reflects on an unprecedented six-decade value investing epoch. Warren Buffett has formally announced that he is stepping down as Chief Executive of Berkshire Hathaway, concluding an extraordinary six-decade tenure that transformed an ailing New England textile mill into a globally revered $1 trillion conglomerate. Reflecting on his departure, Buffett stated simply that 'Father Time always wins,' handing total executive and operational authority to Vice Chairman Greg Abel, who has long overseen the company's vast non-insurance operations including BNSF Railway and Berkshire Hathaway Energy. Buffett’s departure marks the definitive close of an unmatched epoch in global capital markets and value investing philosophy. Under his stewardship, Berkshire delivered compounded annual returns exceeding 20% across six decades, outstripping the S&P 500 by a wide margin through disciplined capital allocation, fortress balance-sheet reserves, and investments in enduring American and global franchises such as Apple, Coca-Cola, and American Express. The company currently holds an unprecedented cash and Treasury-bill war chest exceeding $300 billion, providing Abel with immense liquidity to deploy across future market cycles.

Sunday's Premier League fixtures delivered breathtaking drama across London and Merseyside. At the Emirates Stadium, Arsenal claimed bragging rights in the London derby with a pulsating 2-1 victory over Chelsea. After Morgan Rogers stunned the home crowd with an opening goal in the second minute for Chelsea, Kai Havertz leveled in the 25th minute with a clinical finish before Gunners captain Martin Ødegaard netted the match-winner in the 50th minute before 60,340 fans. On Merseyside, Manchester United battled back from behind to snatch an electrifying 2-2 draw against Everton at Goodison Park. Second-half goals from Bryan Mbeumo (46') and a thunderous header from Benjamin Šeško in the 88th minute rescued a vital road point after Everton had seized the lead through Harrison Armstrong and Tyrique George.
